title: Sheaf presentation by a covering set of sheafified representables
statement: Let $\mathcal D$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $E\subseteq\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal D)$ be a set such that every object of $\mathcal D$ has a covering by objects of $E$. For $V\in E$ put $h_V(W)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(W,V)$, with restriction by precomposition, and let $h_V^\#$ be its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Every sheaf of sets $H$ on $\mathcal D$ admits a coequalizer diagram $P_1\rightrightarrows P_0\to H$ in $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$, where $P_i=\coprod_{j\in J_i}h_{V_{i,j}}^\#$ for sets $J_i$ and objects $V_{i,j}\in E$, for $i=0,1$. Coproducts and coequalizers are colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; the coequalizer assertion means that, for every sheaf $K$, composition induces a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}(H,K)$ to the set of maps $P_0\to K$ whose composites with the two maps $P_1\to P_0$ agree.

proof.text: For every object $V$ and sheaf $T$, the sheafification existence theorem supplies $h_V^\#$ and its unit $\eta_V:h_V\to h_V^\#$. The universal property and the Yoneda bijection give $\operatorname{Hom}(h_V^\#,T)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(h_V,T)\cong T(V)$. The map corresponding to $t\in T(V)$ is characterized by sending $\eta_V(\mathrm{id}_V)$ to $t$; before sheafification it sends $f:W\to V$ to $T(f)(t)$. This also specifies the maps when the site is not subcanonical.

source.place: Tag 00WS, lemma-sheaf-coequalizer-representable, first paragraph; equation-map-representable-into-sheaf preceding Tag 00WR, using Theorem 00WB and Proposition 00WH

proof.text: For an arbitrary sheaf $T$, let $J(T)=\{(V,t):V\in E,\ t\in T(V)\}$, a set since the site is small and all values are sets. Define the presheaf $A_T(W)=\coprod_{(V,t)\in J(T)}\operatorname{Hom}(W,V)$ with restriction $(V,t,f)\mapsto(V,t,f\circ g)$ along $g:W^{\prime}\to W$, and put $P(T)=A_T^\#$. The functor laws follow from associativity and identities in $\mathcal D$. A map $A_T\to K$ to any sheaf $K$ is exactly a family of maps $h_V\to K$, one for each $(V,t)$: restrict to each summand for one direction, and use these maps on disjoint-union elements for the other. Factoring through sheafification on both sides therefore identifies maps $P(T)\to K$ with families of maps $h_V^\#\to K$. The summand inclusion $h_V\to A_T\to P(T)$ factors uniquely through a map $\iota_{V,t}:h_V^\#\to P(T)$. The preceding correspondence sends $b:P(T)\to K$ to $(b\circ\iota_{V,t})_{(V,t)}$, so it proves the coproduct universal property for these injections, including an empty coproduct. The maps of step 1 indexed by $(V,t)$ induce $q_T:P(T)\to T$; on the image of $(V,t,f)$ in $P(T)(W)$ this map is $T(f)(t)$.

source.place: Tag 00WS, first paragraph, displayed coproduct; Tag 00WI, lemma-colimit-sheaves, universal property specialized to coproducts

proof.text: The map $q_T$ is locally surjective. Indeed, for $s\in T(W)$ choose a covering $\{V_i\xrightarrow{f_i}W\}_i$ with $V_i\in E$. In the summand indexed by $(V_i,T(f_i)(s))$, the image of $\mathrm{id}_{V_i}$ under $A_T(V_i)\to P(T)(V_i)$ maps under $q_T$ to $T(f_i)(s)$. This is exactly the covering-local lifting condition, so the sheaf epimorphism criterion implies $q_T$ is an epimorphism. This argument works for every sheaf $T$, so it can be used twice without an additional hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 00WS, first paragraph, epimorphism assertion; Tag 00WN, lemma-mono-epi-sheaves

proof.text: Apply the construction to $T=H$ and write $P_0=P(H)$ and $q=q_H$. Form $G=P_0\times_H P_0$ in sheaves of sets with projections $r,s:G\rightrightarrows P_0$. The sectionwise-limits theorem supplies this fibre product, with $G(W)=\{(a,b)\in P_0(W)^2:q_W(a)=q_W(b)\}$. Apply steps 1--3 to the sheaf $G$ to obtain $P_1=P(G)$ and the epimorphism $e=q_G:P_1\to G$. Both $P_0$ and $P_1$ are coproducts of the stipulated sheafified representables indexed by the sets $J(H)$ and $J(G)$. Put $d_0=r\circ e$ and $d_1=s\circ e$. The fibre-product equation gives $q\circ d_0=q\circ d_1$.

source.place: Tag 00WS, second paragraph, construction of the fibre product and its presentation; Tag 00W2, lemma-limit-sheaf

proof.text: Since $q$ is an epimorphism and $(G,r,s)$ is its kernel pair in the category of sheaves of sets, the kernel-pair coequalizer theorem says that $(H,q)$ is a coequalizer of $r,s$. All its hypotheses hold by steps 3 and 4; the index category used to construct $G$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 086K, lemma-coequalizer-surjection, invoked at the end of Tag 00WS

proof.text: For a sheaf $K$ and a map $a:P_0\to K$ with $a\circ d_0=a\circ d_1$, we have $(a\circ r)\circ e=(a\circ s)\circ e$. As $e$ is an epimorphism, $a\circ r=a\circ s$. Step 5 gives exactly one $u:H\to K$ with $u\circ q=a$. Conversely, every such composite $u\circ q$ equalizes $d_0,d_1$ because $q\circ d_0=q\circ d_1$. These two operations are inverse, which is the stated bijection and the coequalizer universal property. No new coequalizer-existence result is needed: its vertex is the given sheaf $H$.

source.place: Tag 00WS, final sentence, with the universal property of Tag 086K written out after precomposing the kernel pair by an epimorphism
